scope: Claim-level records, primary abstracts/excerpts and named historical documents; not full rereading of every book. Private memories remain author testimony.
alice_status: Prose retained from incoming draft pending separate discussion; sources do not validate its current IIT/whole-city inference.

notes.text: John F. Kennedy, [address on the first anniversary of the Alliance for Progress](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-the-first-anniversary-the-alliance-for-progress), 13 March 1962.
notes.verification: Quotation and date checked against the speech transcript.
notes.locator: Paragraph beginning “Those who possess wealth and power”.

notes.text: James S. Coleman, [*Foundations of Social Theory*](https://www.fulcrum.org/concern/monographs/cr56n1673) (Harvard University Press, 1990), especially the treatments of trust, social capital, and the emergence of norms. The linked digitization is the later paperback edition.
notes.verification: 1990 publication and relevant chapter contents checked; compact summary, not a claim to have reread the entire treatise.

notes.text: Mike Davis, [*City of Quartz: Excavating the Future in Los Angeles*](https://www.versobooks.com/products/1320-city-of-quartz) (Verso, 1990), especially “Fortress L.A.” Later editions are linked. The fortress is Davis’s critical interpretation of the city, not a claim that its inhabitants had no other relationships.
notes.verification: Publication record and named argument checked; not an exhaustive historical audit of the book.

notes.text: Spielberg confirmed USC’s rejection in [a contemporary interview](https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1984/11/19/uscs-new-film-factory/137949f3-4ba5-4284-be4a-670e472b3c11/).
notes.verification: Reported first-person confirmation; no claim about the private neighbor beyond the author’s recollection.

notes.text: Christian List and Philip Pettit, [*Group Agency: The Possibility, Design, and Status of Corporate Agents*](https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199591565.001.0001) (Oxford University Press, 2011), introduction and “The Conditions of Agency.” Their account concerns organized agency; it does not settle whether a group has phenomenal experience.
notes.verification: Source supports organized group agency, not the retained Alice sentence categorically denying group experience. Alice revision is pending author discussion.

notes.text: M. E. J. Newman, [“Modularity and community structure in networks”](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0602124), *PNAS* 103 (2006): 8577–8582, doi:10.1073/pnas.0601602103. Modularity compares within-group connections with a specified null model. It measures neither agency nor consciousness; the application to Los Angeles here is qualitative.
notes.verification: Paper identity and modularity account checked; no Los Angeles network data supplied. Alice interpretation remains under review.

notes.text: Mark S. Granovetter, [“The Strength of Weak Ties”](https://doi.org/10.1086/225469), *American Journal of Sociology* 78 (1973): 1360–1380. For the distinction between bonding and bridging social capital, see Robert D. Putnam, *Bowling Alone* (Simon & Schuster, 2000). A weak tie is not necessarily a bridge, and a bridge does not guarantee trust.
notes.verification: Classic argument and record checked; the city-level application is interpretation.
notes.locator: Granovetter’s discussion of local bridges and diffusion; Putnam, bonding/bridging distinction.

notes.text: Stephen D. Reicher, [“The St. Pauls’ riot: An explanation of the limits of crowd action in terms of a social identity model”](https://doi.org/10.1002/ejsp.2420140102), *European Journal of Social Psychology* 14 (1984): 1–21; John Drury and Stephen Reicher, [“Collective psychological empowerment as a model of social change: Researching crowds and power”](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-4560.2009.01622.x), *Journal of Social Issues* 65 (2009): 707–725. These accounts explain patterned collective action through social identity, not a loss of all individual judgment. The adjacent IIT extrapolation is the author’s open question, not a finding of these studies. For IIT’s actual causal and exclusion requirements, see Larissa Albantakis et al., [“Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0”](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011465), *PLOS Computational Biology* 19 (2023): e1011465.
notes.verification: Research supports identity-sensitive collective action; neither study establishes whole-city integration or an IIT crowd mind. Alice prose deliberately held pending discussion.
notes.locator: St Pauls analysis of boundaries and targets; IIT 4.0 causal/exclusion postulates.

notes.text: R. I. M. Dunbar, Valerio Arnaboldi, Marco Conti and Andrea Passarella, [“The structure of online social networks mirrors those in the offline world”](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3Abea66918-1023-4e17-88d2-b66e1ce71f24), *Social Networks* 43 (2015): 39–47. Observed interaction layers are not a fixed limit on account contacts.
notes.verification: Author repository record and reported layered-network finding checked.

notes.text: Richard Sosis and Eric R. Bressler, [“Cooperation and Commune Longevity: A Test of the Costly Signaling Theory of Religion”](https://www.cognitionandculture.net/wp-content/uploads/Sosis_2003_CommuneLongevity.pdf), *Cross-Cultural Research* 37 (2003): 211–239. In their historical sample of 83 communes, more costly requirements predicted longer survival among religious communes, not secular ones. This is an association, not proof that suffering or difficult entry causes cohesion. The study extends Sosis’s 2000 preliminary comparison.
notes.verification: Full paper checked for study scope, religion interaction, and association. Corrects incoming citation to 2000 alone; “easy entry” in held Alice still needs adjustment.
notes.locator: Results and discussion, religious versus secular requirements.

notes.text: Émile Durkheim, *The Division of Labor in Society* (1893), Book I, on mechanical and organic solidarity; Book III, on abnormal forms of the division of labor. See the [primary-text excerpts](https://us.sagepub.com/sites/default/files/upm-binaries/65238_Edles_Chapter_3.pdf), translated by George Simpson.
notes.verification: Concept and edition/excerpt record checked; full current-host PDF retrieval unavailable. The original text’s abnormal-forms distinction prevents equating interdependence with justice.
notes.locator: Book I, chapters II–III; Book III.

notes.text: Karl Marx, [preface to *A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy*](https://www.marxists.org/archive/marx/works/1859/critique-pol-economy/preface.htm) (1859), on relations of production, property, political forms and conflict. The application to Los Angeles is the narrator’s.
notes.verification: Primary text inspected; no claim that the source proves this particular history.
notes.locator: Paragraphs on material conditions, relations of production and conflict.

notes.text: Max Weber, [*Economy and Society*](https://www.ucpress.edu/book/9780520280021/economy-and-society) (1922; English edition edited by Guenther Roth and Claus Wittich, 1968), Part I, chapter III, “The Types of Legitimate Domination,” especially §2. These are ideal types of claimed legitimacy, not a certification of any authority’s fairness.
notes.verification: Publisher record and primary excerpt checked; causal application is the narrator’s.

notes.text: Erving Goffman, [*The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life*](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/61106/the-presentation-of-self-in-everyday-life-by-erving-goffman/) (1956; revised US edition, 1959), especially “Performances” and “Regions and Region Behavior.”
notes.verification: Publisher description/edition and relevant chapter concepts checked.

notes.text: Cristina Bicchieri, [*The Grammar of Society: The Nature and Dynamics of Social Norms*](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/grammar-of-society/2B063E9C9621C2340DEFB2BE15B3AEA5) (Cambridge University Press, 2006), chapter 1, on conditional preferences, empirical and normative expectations, and pluralistic ignorance. Her [diagnostic framework with Ryan Muldoon and Alessandro Sontuoso](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01418/full) distinguishes social norms from practices maintained by other incentives.
notes.verification: Primary conceptual account checked; examples are explanatory, not invented memoir.

notes.text: R. I. M. Dunbar, [“Neocortex size as a constraint on group size in primates”](https://doi.org/10.1016/0047-2484(92)90081-J), *Journal of Human Evolution* 22 (1992): 469–493; for layered relationships, Dunbar, [“Structure and function in human and primate social networks”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7482201/) (2020). For the uncertainty of extrapolating a human limit, see Patrik Lindenfors, Andreas Wartel and Johan Lind, [“‘Dunbar’s number’ deconstructed”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8103230/), *Biology Letters* 17 (2021): 20210158.
notes.verification: Original hypothesis, observed layer account and critical reanalysis checked; no fixed 150-person ceiling asserted.
notes.locator: Primate regression; human network layers; 2021 results/confidence intervals.

notes.text: Damon Centola and Michael Macy, [“Complex Contagions and the Weakness of Long Ties”](https://ndg.asc.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Centola-Macy-2007-AJS.pdf), *American Journal of Sociology* 113 (2007): 702–734, doi:10.1086/521848. Their network model distinguishes transmission through one contact from adoption requiring multiple reinforcing contacts.
notes.verification: Primary model and abstract inspected; illustrative workplace extension is not a claim about a tested labor intervention.

notes.text: Émile Durkheim, [*The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life*](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/41360/pg41360-images.html) (1912), Book II, chapter VII; English translation by Joseph Ward Swain (1915). “Collective effervescence” is his theoretical interpretation of collective ritual.
notes.verification: Primary edition and relevant theoretical account checked; not treated as a universal experimental law.

notes.text: Victor Turner, [*The Ritual Process: Structure and Anti-Structure*](https://www.routledge.com/The-Ritual-Process-Structure-and-Anti-Structure/Turner/p/book/9781315134666) (1969), chapter 3, “Liminality and Communitas,” building on Arnold van Gennep’s *The Rites of Passage* (1909). The fraternity comparison is the narrator’s.
notes.verification: Publisher chapter record and primary excerpt located; analogy distinguished from an observed Turner fraternity study.

notes.text: Elliot Aronson and Judson Mills, [“The effect of severity of initiation on liking for a group”](https://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/15341_Readings/Motivation/Aronson_Mills_1959_The_effect_of_severity_of_initiation.pdf), *Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology* 59 (1959): 177–181. The outcome was a rating of the group, not durable solidarity. For a longitudinal fraternity test, see Aldo Cimino and Benjamin J. Thomas, [“Does hazing actually increase group solidarity? Re-examining a classic theory with a modern fraternity”](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1090513822000423), *Evolution and Human Behavior* 43 (2022): 408–417.
notes.verification: 1959 primary methods/results inspected; 2022 bibliographic record and study findings checked.
notes.locator: 1959 methods and rating outcome; 2022 six-cohort longitudinal analysis.

notes.text: Jessica C. Flack, Michelle Girvan, Frans B. M. de Waal and David C. Krakauer, [“Policing stabilizes construction of social niches in primates”](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04326), *Nature* 439 (2006): 426–429. Temporary removal of key conflict interveners in one captive pigtailed-macaque group changed its social networks. This supports a bounded comparison, not a biological prescription for human hierarchy.
notes.verification: Primary-paper bibliographic and experimental findings checked; single-troop scope explicit.

notes.text: Robert J. Sampson, Stephen W. Raudenbush and Felton Earls, [“Neighborhoods and Violent Crime: A Multilevel Study of Collective Efficacy”](https://dash.harvard.edu/entities/publication/73120378-bd4a-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b), *Science* 277 (1997): 918–924. The study of 343 Chicago neighborhoods reports an adjusted association; it does not randomly assign trust or intervention.
notes.verification: Author repository abstract and study design checked.

notes.text: Pierre Bourdieu, [*Distinction: A Social Critique of the Judgement of Taste*](https://books.google.com/books/about/Distinction.html?id=nVaS6gS9Jz4C) (1979), translated by Richard Nice (Harvard University Press, 1984), especially “The Habitus and the Space of Life-Styles.” Habitus includes learned dispositions of perception and action; the personal example is an interpretation, not a diagnosis.
notes.verification: Edition and conceptual account checked; no claim to have reread the full book.

notes.text: Raj Chetty, Nathaniel Hendren and Lawrence F. Katz, [“The Effects of Exposure to Better Neighborhoods on Children: New Evidence from the Moving to Opportunity Experiment”](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20150572), *American Economic Review* 106 (2016): 855–902. Benefits depended on age at move; the findings for young children should not be generalized to every mover. The experiment does not isolate friendship as the mechanism.
notes.verification: Primary abstract and randomized-voucher design checked.

notes.text: Raj Chetty et al., [“Social capital II: determinants of economic connectedness”](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04997-3), *Nature* 608 (2022): 122–134. The analysis separates exposure to higher-income people from friendship formation conditional on that exposure. Its Facebook-based measures and decompositions do not make every observed association a causal effect.
notes.verification: Primary methods and decomposition checked.

notes.text: [*Report of the Independent Commission on the Los Angeles Police Department*](https://scalar.usc.edu/works/the-los-angeles-riots-christopher-and-webster-commissions-collections/media/Independent_Commission_Report.pdf) (Christopher Commission, July 1991), especially the findings on excessive force, racial bias and mobile-data-terminal messages.
notes.verification: Contemporary commission report and USC archive description checked.
notes.locator: Summary and chapters on force and racism/bias.

notes.text: Harlins was killed on 16 March 1991; the conviction was on 11 October, and sentencing on 15 November. See [*People v. Superior Court (Du)*, 5 Cal. App. 4th 822 (1992)](https://law.justia.com/cases/california/court-of-appeal/4th/5/822.html), for the offense, voluntary-manslaughter verdict and suspended prison sentence, and contemporary reports of [the conviction](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-10-12-mn-152-story.html) and [sentencing](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-11-16-mn-1402-story.html).
notes.verification: Court opinion checked; dates cross-checked to contemporary reports. The incoming November-conviction claim was wrong.

notes.text: Elijah Anderson, [*Code of the Street: Decency, Violence, and the Moral Life of the Inner City*](https://elijahanderson.com/code-of-the-street/) (W. W. Norton, 1999). His ethnography concerns Philadelphia; it supplies a mechanism for comparison, not a survey of the narrator’s Los Angeles neighborhood. Residents need not endorse the street code to face pressure to navigate it.
notes.verification: Author description and ethnographic scope checked.
notes.locator: Author’s account of decent/street orientations and respect.

notes.text: Andrew M. Guess et al., [“How do social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior in an election campaign?”](https://csdp.princeton.edu/publications/how-do-social-media-feed-algorithms-affect-attitudes-and-behavior-election-campaign), *Science* 381 (2023): 398–404, doi:10.1126/science.abp9364. The intervention changed feeds for consenting users during the 2020 US election. Its three-month null findings on measured attitudes are not evidence that ranking has no effects in other settings or over longer periods.
notes.verification: Author-institution abstract inspected, including changed exposure/time and nonsignificant attitude effects.

notes.text: Hirokazu Shirado and Nicholas A. Christakis, [“Locally noisy autonomous agents improve global human coordination in network experiments”](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature22332), *Nature* 545 (2017): 370–374. The task was network coloring; benefits depended on bot placement and the amount of noise. These were simple software agents, not present-day language models.
notes.verification: Primary abstract and experimental summary checked.
notes.locator: Coloring task; central placement/moderate noise and spillovers.

notes.text: Ariel Flint Ashery, Luca Maria Aiello and Andrea Baronchelli, [“Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12077490/), *Science Advances* 11 (2025): eadu9368, doi:10.1126/sciadv.adu9368. Agents interacted through a researcher-defined naming game with specified incentives and memory. The finding concerns conventions and preferences in that task, not spontaneous humanlike consciousness or proof of human social behavior.
notes.verification: Primary methods excerpt and results abstract inspected; task scaffolding retained explicitly.
notes.locator: Naming-game methods, convergence and collective bias.

notes.text: [USC’s football record against UCLA](https://usctrojans.com/sports/football/opponent-history/ucla/13) lists the 37–38 loss at Pasadena on 21 November 1992. The [USC media guide](https://usctrojans.com/documents/download/2004/7/21/04-mg-137-211.pdf) records the unsuccessful late two-point attempt. The passage deliberately flashes forward beyond the April unrest. Overtime entered Division I-A regular-season football in 1996; it had existed earlier in other college contexts.
notes.verification: Team record and historical game account checked; author confirms attendance.
notes.locator: 1992 season game account and opponent-history row.

notes.text: Muzafer Sherif, O. J. Harvey, B. Jack White, William R. Hood and Carolyn W. Sherif, [*Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The Robbers Cave Experiment*](https://psychclassics.yorku.ca/Sherif/chap8.htm) (1961), reporting the 1954 camp study. Rivalry was deliberately cultivated; a series of goals requiring cooperation helped reduce it. This was a small, selected group of boys in a researcher-managed setting.
notes.verification: Original report’s conclusions inspected; selection and orchestration limits preserved.
notes.locator: Chapter 8, conclusions on competition and superordinate goals.

notes.text: Magic Johnson announced his HIV diagnosis on 7 November 1991; Freddie Mercury died on 24 November. See the [US government’s HIV/AIDS timeline](https://www.hiv.gov/hiv-basics/overview/history/hiv-and-aids-timeline), 1991 entries. The freeway, radio sequence and tears are personal recollection.
notes.verification: Public dates corroborated; private scene is not externally certified.

notes.text: [*Koon v. United States*, 518 U.S. 81 (1996)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supct/html/94-1664.ZO.html), part I, recounts the 29 April 1992 state acquittals and the deadlocked count against Laurence Powell. Stacey Koon and Powell were convicted in the later federal civil-rights trial.
notes.verification: Supreme Court factual history inspected.
notes.locator: Part I, state and federal proceedings.

notes.text: The [USC Libraries’ account of its commission archives](https://libraries.usc.edu/article/usc-libraries-digitizing-150000-pages-records-related-1991-king-beating-1992-riots) reports 58 deaths, 2,383 injuries and about $1 billion in damage. Later counts differ. The text therefore uses broad casualty language and does not equate every damaged building with one burned down.
notes.verification: Archive’s figures checked; variable totals deliberately not harmonized into false precision.

notes.text: US Commission on Civil Rights, [*Racial and Ethnic Tensions in American Communities: Poverty, Inequality, and Discrimination, Volume V: The Los Angeles Report*](https://www.usccr.gov/files/historical/1999/99-014.pdf) (1999), on the unrest, Korean American businesses, law-enforcement failures and intercommunity relations. These experiences cannot be reduced to one uniform conflict between two populations.
notes.verification: Official retrospective report located and relevant account checked in the historical review; not a claim to have reread all testimony.

notes.text: USC’s commencement was on 8 May 1992, nine days after the verdict: [contemporary report](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-05-09-me-1626-story.html), 9 May 1992.
notes.verification: Date checked; author confirms attendance and subdued atmosphere.
